steps: This video shows how a canary rollout catches a quality drop before it reaches everyone. Before any traffic moves, you send thresholds to the rollback gate: revert if accuracy drops more than two points or hallucination rises one point, from a ninety-five point eight percent baseline.
In stage one, you hand the hybrid retrieval release to the traffic splitter, which routes it to five percent of clinicians for forty-eight hours.

After forty-eight hours, the splitter reports the canary's metrics to the gate: ninety-six point two percent accuracy and one point eight percent hallucination. That passes, so the gate widens the canary to twenty-five percent.
Stage two also passes, at ninety-six point one percent accuracy and one point nine percent hallucination. The gate widens the canary to fifty percent for twenty-four hours.
At fifty percent, accuracy falls to ninety-three point two percent, a drop of two point six points. That is over the two point limit, so the gate marks the threshold breached.
Rollback is automatic. The gate tells the splitter to revert all traffic to the baseline, back to one hundred percent, and pages the on-call S R E with an accuracy regression alert.

On-call follows the runbook and escalates to you. Half the clinicians never saw the regression, and you trace it to rare claim types, then refine the re-ranker and re-test. Takeaway: set rollback thresholds first, then widen traffic in stages. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
